title: Digital Asset Pipeline & Interchange Core v1

domain.name: Digital Asset Pipeline & Interchange
domain.description: Cross-program 3D asset pipeline skills for units, coordinates, file formats, naming, versioning, mesh/runtime preparation, textures, rigs, animation transfer, engine validation, automation, and quality control.

competencies.name: Units, Coordinates & Scale Conventions
competencies.description: Control real-world scale, up-axis, handedness, origins, pivots, and coordinate conventions across tools.
competencies.purpose: Prevent systematic placement and export errors between DCCs, GIS sources, and game engines.

units.title: Coordinate mismatches compound across a pipeline
units.content: Meters versus centimeters, Y-up versus Z-up, local versus world space, handedness, and pivot conventions can each create correct-looking single assets that fail when assembled together.

units.title: Coordinate contract
units.content: Define authoritative units, world origin policy, up-axis, forward direction, pivot rules, and geographic offset if relevant; document conversions per tool; test with a reference cube or known-distance asset before exporting a full batch.

units.title: Coordinate failures
units.content: Avoid fixing every imported asset with ad hoc scale multipliers, changing world origin after placement, mixing centered and placement-ready pivots without labels, and assuming two tools interpret forward/up identically.

drills.title: Validate a cross-tool scale contract
drills.prompt: Design a reference test that proves a Blender asset, Unity import, and Unreal import all agree on dimensions, pivot, up axis, and forward direction.

competencies.name: 3D Formats, Export & Import
competencies.description: Choose and validate FBX, glTF/GLB, OBJ, USD-family, image, cache, and related interchange formats based on asset needs.
competencies.purpose: Preserve the data that matters while avoiding unsupported assumptions during transfer.

units.title: File formats preserve different kinds of truth
units.content: Geometry, materials, hierarchy, animation, cameras, lights, units, custom attributes, and instancing are preserved differently by each interchange format. The best format depends on the production contract, not familiarity alone.

units.title: Format selection workflow
units.content: List required data; identify target-tool support; choose simplest format that preserves those requirements; define export presets; import a small representative asset; compare scale, normals, materials, hierarchy, animation, and metadata before batch transfer.

units.title: Interchange failures
units.content: Avoid assuming materials transfer perfectly, changing export settings asset by asset, using OBJ when rigs or hierarchy are required, and batch-exporting before testing a representative complex asset.

drills.title: Choose an interchange format
drills.prompt: Select a transfer strategy for a static environment kit, an animated character, and a scene that must preserve hierarchy and metadata.

competencies.name: Naming, Versioning & Asset Provenance
competencies.description: Track stable asset IDs, source files, export versions, ownership, references, and derived outputs.
competencies.purpose: Know where every runtime asset came from and which source should be edited.

units.title: Asset identity workflow
units.content: Assign stable asset name/ID; separate source, intermediate, and runtime outputs; include version or revision where appropriate; record creator/source/reference and licensing notes; preserve links from exported asset back to editable source; avoid overwriting approved runtime files without traceability.

units.title: Source of truth should be obvious
units.content: When two files look authoritative, people eventually edit the wrong one. Make editable source, generated output, and approved runtime artifact roles explicit in paths and naming.

units.title: Provenance failures
units.content: Avoid final_final2 naming, duplicating source meshes into many folders with no ownership, overwriting exports manually without revision history, and losing the reference or license trail for downloaded assets.

drills.title: Design an asset provenance map
drills.prompt: Create naming and folder rules for a real-world building that has GIS source, photo references, Blender source, textures, and Unity/Unreal runtime exports.

competencies.name: Mesh, LOD, Collision & Runtime Preparation
competencies.description: Prepare geometry for runtime use with appropriate topology, normals, LODs, instancing, collision, and bounds.
competencies.purpose: Deliver assets that work efficiently and predictably in real-time engines.

units.title: Runtime mesh checklist
units.content: Validate scale and transforms; remove accidental hidden geometry; inspect normals/tangents; limit material slots; define LOD or simplification strategy; create collision appropriate to interaction; verify bounds/pivot; test repeated instances in target engine.

units.title: Collision and visual geometry solve different problems
units.content: Collision should represent gameplay/physics needs with the simplest reliable shape. Matching every visual triangle usually wastes runtime cost and may create unstable interaction.

units.title: Runtime mesh failures
units.content: Avoid hero-detail geometry on distant repeated assets, convex collision that changes important walkable shape without testing, accidental material-slot multiplication, and LOD transitions that alter silhouette or collision unexpectedly.

drills.title: Prepare a street kit for runtime
drills.prompt: Define runtime mesh, LOD, collision, and material-slot rules for repeated curbs, sidewalks, poles, walls, and storefront modules.

competencies.name: Textures, Color Space & Channel Packing
competencies.description: Manage texture resolution, compression, linear versus color data, normal maps, packed channels, atlases, and memory budgets.
competencies.purpose: Preserve surface meaning while reducing memory and transfer mistakes.

units.title: Not every texture is color
units.content: Base color/emissive images and numeric data such as roughness, metallic, AO, masks, height, and normal maps require different color-space and compression assumptions. Incorrect import settings alter material meaning.

units.title: Texture delivery workflow
units.content: Define texture roles and naming; set target texel density/resolution; choose packing convention; export appropriate bit depth and color space; verify normal-map orientation; import with matching compression/data settings; inspect memory and visual result in target engine.

units.title: Texture pipeline failures
units.content: Avoid treating packed masks as color, inconsistent channel conventions across assets, oversized unique textures for repeated props, and fixing color-space mistakes by changing shader values instead of correcting import/data interpretation.

drills.title: Define a shared texture contract
drills.prompt: Create a texture naming, channel-packing, color-space, normal-map, and resolution policy for assets moving from Blender into Unity and Unreal.

competencies.name: Rig & Animation Transfer
competencies.description: Transfer skeletons, skinning, clips, root motion, frame rates, and retargetable animation between authoring tools and engines.
competencies.purpose: Preserve deformation and motion intent across application boundaries.

units.title: Animation export contract
units.content: Confirm rest pose and scale; identify deform bones; define root-motion policy; set frame range and frame rate; bake required constraints; export one known clip; validate bone orientation, animation curves, root behavior, and retargeting in target engine before batch export.

units.title: Skeleton consistency matters more than per-clip fixes
units.content: If each animation needs a unique import hack, the skeleton/export contract is likely inconsistent. Fix the shared root cause before expanding the animation library.

units.title: Animation transfer failures
units.content: Avoid exporting control/helper bones unintentionally, mismatched rest poses, inconsistent frame rates, double-applied root motion, and batch-converting clips before validating one representative animation.

drills.title: Validate an animation in two engines
drills.prompt: Design a Blender export test that proves one skeletal clip preserves scale, skeleton, timing, and root behavior in both Unity and Unreal.

competencies.name: Engine Import & Validation
competencies.description: Create repeatable import checks for scale, materials, normals, collision, animation, naming, dependencies, and performance.
competencies.purpose: Catch transfer failures at the boundary before they multiply across many assets.

units.title: Import validation gate
units.content: Import into a designated test scene; verify scale and pivot against a known reference; inspect normals and materials; check texture assignments; test collision and animation; inspect bounds and LODs; place multiple instances; profile representative cost; accept or return with specific failure reason.

units.title: Validate a representative asset before a batch
units.content: A single complex asset containing the common edge cases reveals pipeline problems far more cheaply than discovering the same error across hundreds of exports.

units.title: Validation failures
units.content: Avoid accepting assets based only on viewport appearance, skipping collision and scale tests, hiding bad normals with two-sided materials, and batch-fixing import settings manually with no shared preset.

drills.title: Create an engine import gate
drills.prompt: Define pass/fail checks for environment assets entering Unity or Unreal from Blender.

competencies.name: Pipeline Automation & Quality Control
competencies.description: Automate validation, export, naming, conversion, and reporting while preserving source safety and traceability.
competencies.purpose: Scale asset throughput without turning silent mistakes into mass-produced failures.

units.title: Safe pipeline automation
units.content: Automate only after the manual contract is known; validate inputs; operate on copies or generated outputs; emit deterministic names and logs; fail loudly on invalid assets; preserve source files; make reruns idempotent where practical; version automation with the project.

units.title: Automation should reject bad input, not normalize everything silently
units.content: Silent repairs hide upstream inconsistency. Validation should distinguish safe automatic normalization from conditions that require human review.

units.title: Automation failures
units.content: Avoid batch scripts that overwrite sources, swallow errors, export partially valid assets, depend on active UI selection with no checks, and continue after a coordinate or naming contract fails.

drills.title: Design a batch export and QC tool
drills.prompt: Plan an automation that validates Blender assets, exports engine-ready copies, writes a report, and stops safely on contract violations.
